1	# Task 1: rotating PBR cube with orbit control
2	
3	Build a scene with Aura3D (`@aura3d/engine`, already installed in node_modules).
4	
5	Requirements:
6	1. One cube with a physically based (PBR) material: visibly metallic and rough (not a flat unlit colour).
7	2. Lighting that makes the cube clearly readable (key light plus fill or environment), on a dark-grey background.
8	3. The cube rotates continuously by itself.
9	4. The user can drag with the mouse to orbit the camera around the cube (orbit control), including while it rotates.
10	5. Camera framing shows the whole cube centred.
11	
12	The rendering contract in the next section applies.
13	
14	## Rendering contract (all tasks)
15	
16	- Draw into the existing `<canvas id="app">` (640x360 CSS pixels, device pixel ratio 1). Do not resize it or create another canvas.
17	- Render continuously with `requestAnimationFrame`. When the first frame has been drawn set `window.__EVAL_READY__ = true`.
18	- No network access: load assets only from `/assets/...` (served from `public/assets`). Do not import from CDNs.
19	- Code goes in `src/` (TypeScript, strict). The entry is `src/main.ts`. It must pass `typecheck` and build with `vite build`.
20	- When you are done, call `finish`.
21

4	HUD, touch, audio, a fixed-step loop and a safety net ship in the same install, so a game needs no extra libraries.

7	Aura3D is a TypeScript engine API (`@aura3d/engine`), an asset CLI (`@aura3d/cli`), templates (`create-aura3d`) and a deploy checker. You write declarative scene source; `createAuraApp` owns the renderer, camera, frame loop and resize. Do not import `three`, write a loader or add a render loop.

9	Read first: [`threejs-to-aura3d.md`](threejs-to-aura3d.md) (if you would write X in three.js, write Y; every line type-checked), then this page, then [`recipes.md`](recipes.md) (a complete scene for the common tasks: copy it, then adapt) and `docs/agents/claims-and-boundaries.md`. input.summary: I wrote src/main.ts, adapted from recipe 1 in docs/agents/recipes.md. It builds a metallic, rough PBR box (metallic 0.9, roughness 0.38) on a dark-grey (#2b2b2e) background. The scene has neutral environment light, a shadowed key light and a blue-tinted fill light. The cube rotates each frame in `onFrame`. `interactions.orbit` handles mouse-drag orbit, and the orbit camera is placed to show the whole cube centred. `window.__EVAL_READY__` is set on the second frame callback. The typecheck passes. I didn't run `vite build` (no shell), and I never saw the scene render in a browser.
